lines.en: Tom, look at the park. It’s so clean now!

lines.en: It was a mess last month. The grass was covered in cans and paper.

lines.en: The playground is clean, too. Children play there every afternoon.

facts.label: Resultado de uma limpeza
facts.sub: Use is/are + adjetivo para o estado agora e was/were + particípio para a ação: The pond was cleaned. Os dois juntos contam uma mudança.

facts.label: está/estão + adjetivo
facts.sub: Use is ou are + adjetivo para o resultado agora: The park is clean. The benches are new. Fale do estado atual e dê detalhes que você vê.

facts.label: foi/foram + particípio
facts.sub: Use was/were + particípio para contar o que foi feito: The pond was cleaned. The flowers were planted. Dá a causa do resultado. Use was com singular e were com plural.

compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “o parque está limpo” e “o parque foi limpo” com estar e ser.
compare.us: Em inglês, use is + adjetivo para o resultado agora: The park is clean. Use was/were + particípio para a ação: The pond was cleaned. O adjetivo mostra o resultado.

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.
group: Leia as duas colunas e peça que apontem a maior diferença.
Pergunta: The park is clean now.
extra90: Dupla: um fala como no Brasil, o outro como nos EUA.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: We use is/are to say how a place looks now.
We use was/were to say what was done before.
We say “The park is cleaned now” for the result.
items.why: We say The park is clean now.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: We use is/are to say how a place looks now. → Verdadeiro (Yes: The park is clean.)
We use was/were to say what was done before. → Verdadeiro (Yes: The pond was cleaned.)
We say “The park is cleaned now” for the result. → Falso (We say The park is clean now.)

pages.title: A park in Dublin · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a bright Saturday in Dublin. Tom and Bree walk into the park. The grass is green and the paths are tidy. A month ago everything looked different. Bree helped to clean the park. Tom wants to hear the whole story.

“Tom, look at the park. It’s so clean now!” says Bree. “It was a mess last month. The grass was covered in cans and paper.” says Tom. “Volunteers cleaned it on Saturday. The paths are clear and the benches are new.” says Bree.
